Actionable interpretation

1 · Attack disturbance intensity before adding labour.

Production rate has a materially stronger negative association with disturbance intensity (r = −0.557) than with headcount (r = −0.014). Prioritize the repeated stoppage causes and stabilize the process first.

2 · Review small-batch planning and changeovers.

Q1 orders have the lowest median rate and highest recorded disturbance intensity. Grouping compatible products, reducing setup time and improving changeover standards are likely more relevant than simply pushing line speed.

3 · Use MES and Excel as reconciliation partners, not competing “truths”.

87.1% of matched orders are within ±5% quantity, but only one exact quantity match exists. Focus investigation on the long-tail outliers and timestamp differences rather than treating every small variance equally.

Top type-1 stoppage reasons (2026)

Raw labels show a taxonomy issue: planned-looking labels such as RUHE/Rüsten/Pause appear alongside disturbance labels. Normalize planned vs unplanned before cost attribution.

Workstream B — Production, stoppage and staffing

Goal: explain performance variation, stoppage patterns, staffing effectiveness and MES ↔ Excel consistency.

Order size effect

Median gross rate rises with order size while disturbance intensity declines.

Staffing: throughput vs employee productivity

More workers do not automatically increase line rate; units per employee-hour decline sharply in higher staffing buckets.

What the current energy data can and cannot answer

Supported now

Meter mapping, sample-window energy delta, component contribution, timestamp-overlap allocation method, and a pilot order-level normalization.

Recommended KPI

Allocated energy / 1,000 good units and allocated energy / production hour, tracked by product and order once coverage expands.

Not supported reliably yet

Product energy ranking, density correlation, energy-vs-rate correlation, or stoppage-energy cost by reason. The pilot contains one allocatable order and density is missing for that product.

Data required

Several weeks of continuous KM1 energy, confirmed kWh unit, machine-state timestamps, electricity tariff, reliable density/master data, and a stable order-to-energy allocation window.

Data Quality & Completeness

Data quality is itself a management KPI because it changes the reliability of production and cost conclusions.

Relationship / join coverage

Coverage of the main semantic-model links. Low coverage is a root cause of missing or biased downstream KPIs.

MES ↔ Excel timestamp reconciliation

263 orders have comparable timestamps. The median start-time difference is modest, but the p90 tail is large.

KPI definitions used in this dashboard / Power BI

Gross Production RateProduced Units ÷ Usage Minutes

Order-level throughput including time inside the recorded usage window.

Availability ProxyProduction Seconds ÷ Usage Seconds

Main OEE availability component from MES production periods.

Performance ProxyProduced Units ÷ Σ(Target Units/Min × Production Minutes)

Uses period-level target rates.

Quality Proxy(Produced − Rejects) ÷ Produced

Use with caution until rejection coverage improves.

OEE ProxyAvailability × Performance × Quality

Display as proxy, not certified OEE, while data definitions remain incomplete.

Units / Employee-hourProduced Units ÷ Σ(Worker Count × Usage Hours)

Normalizes output for staffing effort.

MES ↔ Excel Qty Variance %(MES Quantity − Excel Quantity) ÷ Excel Quantity

Use absolute value for consistency thresholds.

Energy / 1,000 UnitsAllocated Meter Delta ÷ (Produced Units ÷ 1,000)

Only valid once meter unit and timestamp allocation are validated.

DAX-ready measure pattern

Names are illustrative; adapt column names to the final Power BI model.
Gross Production Rate := DIVIDE( SUM(FactProductionPeriod[ProducedUnits]), DIVIDE(SUM(FactProductionPeriod[UsageSeconds]),60) ) Availability Proxy := DIVIDE( SUM(FactProductionPeriod[ProductionSeconds]), SUM(FactProductionPeriod[UsageSeconds]) ) Quality Proxy := DIVIDE( [Produced Units] - [Reject Qty], [Produced Units] ) OEE Proxy := [Availability Proxy] * [Performance Proxy] * [Quality Proxy] Units per Employee Hour := DIVIDE( [Produced Units], SUMX(FactProductionPeriod, FactProductionPeriod[AvgWorkers] * FactProductionPeriod[UsageHours]) ) MES vs Excel Qty Variance % := DIVIDE( [MES Produced Qty] - [Excel Produced Qty], [Excel Produced Qty] ) Energy per 1,000 Units := DIVIDE( [Allocated Energy], DIVIDE([Produced Units],1000) ) Stoppage Min per Usage Hour := DIVIDE( [Stoppage Minutes], [Usage Hours] )
